source_doc: Chappell & Co Ltd v Nestle Co Ltd, [1960] AC 87 (HL)
extracted_text: A contracting party can stipulate for what consideration he chooses. A peppercorn does not cease to be good consideration if it is established that the promisee does not like pepper and will throw away the corn.
axiom_summary: Consideration must be sufficient (having some legal value) but need not be adequate (equivalent in economic value to the promise received).
